title: Westbrook School Committee — Special Meeting

fields.Location: Westbrook High School (Room 114), 125 Stroudwater St. (Hybrid via Zoom)

note: This summary highlights the meeting's key discussions and decisions, with direct quotes and timestamps for verification — it is not a substitute for watching the full meeting. All seven members attended (Katy Rice remote); no student representatives attended. The committee voted unanimously at the outset to skip minutes approval, the Superintendent's Report, and committee reports given this special meeting's narrow purpose. For complete context, nuance, and anything not covered, watch the full video at the link above. (Produced by: WestbrookCurrents.com)
attendance: Present: Chair Andrea Mancuso, Vice Chair Katy Rice (remote), Allison Brunette, Erin Cavallaro, Noreen Poitras, Brooke Reed (arrived after roll call), Dr. Flynn Ross.

blocks.x: Old Business: FY27 Budget, Second & Final Reading
11.1 — Adoption of the FY27 Budget, Second and Final Reading (Roll Call Vote)

Before the vote, the committee heard four written public comments. They urged that Westbrook Middle School instructional coach positions be restored to the budget rather than eliminated as proposed. All four praised literacy coach Julie Reardon, and two also named math coach Brianna Morrell.
This continues the same concern raised in public comment at the April 8 meeting. No board member reopened discussion of this line item.
The budget was adopted as presented, without amendment. This was the second and final reading, the last and binding vote.
Approved 7–0 by roll call (second and final reading). Moved by Noreen Poitras, seconded by Allison Brunette.

“I am writing to share my disappointment and heartbreak at hearing that Julie Reardon's position...is planned to be cut from next year's school budget...Julie is more than a salary to be paid, she is an absolutely integral part of the Westbrook Middle School community.”
blocks.cite: Bridget Chapin, sixth-grade ELA teacher (written comment)

blocks.x: “If, through its careful planning, the board can find a way to return the 5 through 12 literacy coach to its budget request...the district would be in a significantly better position to help our students succeed.”

Director of Technology Barbara Morgan negotiated a five-year lease instead of a purchase. The lease has a fixed per-copy rate for the term, including maintenance, toner, and repairs at the user level. This moderates future costs and reduces the district's exposure to a costly equipment failure.
It is already reflected in the adopted FY27 budget. It was taken as a combined first-and-final reading, meaning one vote that serves as both the first reading and the final, binding vote.
Approved 7–0. Mover not stated on the recording. Seconded by Noreen Poitras.
12.2 — Overnight Field Trip: Maine National UN Conference

An overnight trip for six Westbrook High School students to the University of Southern Maine's Gorham campus for the Maine National UN (United Nations) Conference (May 13–15, 2026). The cost is approximately $260 per student, all inclusive. It was taken as a combined first-and-final reading.
Approved 7–0. Mover not stated on the recording. Seconded by Brooke Reed.
An Individual Statement from Chair Mancuso

During the second public-comment period, Chair Mancuso temporarily handed administration of the meeting to Erin Cavallaro. She spoke from the podium in her individual capacity. She spoke as a parent, as an attorney in a leadership role addressing gender-based violence in Maine, and as an individual committee member (not an official committee position).

Cavallaro addressed a Maine legislative hearing scheduled the next day on a proposed act concerning school sports participation and facilities based on gender identity. She stated her intent to submit individual testimony in opposition. She encouraged fellow members to do the same in their own capacities. She cited Maine Integrated Youth Health Survey data on disproportionate harassment and violence faced by LGBTQ-identifying students. No board discussion or action followed.
No vote — individual public comment, not a committee action.
